advancing-bc-homes-housing-needs-in-chil.h1: B.C. Housing Targets in Chilliwack, Mission and the Fraser Valley

parts.t: In March 2024 I wrote that Chilliwack and Mission were about to get provincial housing targets. Both now have them. Here's what the targets are, how the Fraser Valley is tracking, and what it means if you're buying or selling.

Under B.C.'s Housing Supply Act, the Province gives fast-growing municipalities a five-year target for net new homes, with yearly milestones. Cities report progress twice a year, and the Province can step in if a city falls well short and isn't trying. The targets come with other changes: small-scale multi-unit housing on most single-family lots, Transit-Oriented Areas near SkyTrain stations, and faster approvals.
Five-year targets (
Storeys tracker
, August 2025):

items.t: 1,798, from 211 in year one to 1,798 cumulative by year five (

parts.t: After their first full year, Chilliwack had completed 1,069 net new homes against a year-one target of 659, or 162%. Surrey (153%) and Maple Ridge (123%) were also ahead, while Abbotsford (59%) and White Rock (70%) were behind. Mission and the Township of Langley hadn't reported year-one results when that data was published.

items.t: More choice in townhomes and condos.
Targets mean more approvals. Combined with a slower market, buyers in Chilliwack and Mission have more new and resale homes to choose from than a few years ago.

grey-whales-and-orcas-near-south-surrey-.description: Grey whales and orcas off White Rock and Crescent Beach: when they pass, where to watch from shore, and how far boats must stay from them.
grey-whales-and-orcas-near-south-surrey-.h1: Grey Whales and Orcas off White Rock and Crescent Beach

parts.t: In May 2024, over the Mother's Day weekend, a local boater photographed two grey whales close to shore off Crescent Beach, with orcas nearby. It wasn't a one-off. Whales turn up in Semiahmoo Bay and Boundary Bay most years, and seeing one from the beach is one of the things people love about living in South Surrey and White Rock.

items.t: migrate up the coast each spring, from their winter calving lagoons off Baja California and Mexico to feeding grounds in the Bering Sea, and a few stop to feed in the shallow bays. Spring is the best time to look.
come into Boundary Bay and Semiahmoo Bay too. Most seen here are Bigg's (transient) killer whales, which hunt seals and sea lions.
have come back to the Salish Sea in growing numbers and are seen farther out in the Strait of Georgia.
the 470-metre pier gets you well out over the water, and the promenade runs about 2.19 km from East Beach to West Beach.
look west and south across Boundary Bay from the beach and Blackie Spit.
the higher viewpoints, such as Kwomais Point Park, look over Boundary Bay.

parts.t: Bring binoculars, look for a blow first, and check local sighting groups on social media; sightings get posted within minutes.

holden-residences-assignment-sale-jared-.description: Buying or selling a presale condo by assignment in BC: how assignments work, developer consent and fees, GST, and the BC home flipping tax.
holden-residences-assignment-sale-jared-.h1: Assignment Sales in BC: How They Work and What They Cost

parts.t: In 2024 I listed an assignment at Holden Residences in Grandview Heights: a 2 bedroom and den, 954 sq ft, sold before the building completed. Assignments are common in South Surrey and Langley, where so many condos and townhomes are sold as presales. Here's how they work, and the rules that changed since.
When you buy a presale, you sign a contract with the developer for a home that isn't built yet. An
assignment
is selling that contract to someone else before completion. The new buyer (the assignee) takes over your contract and completes the purchase with the developer when the building is finished.

items.t: most presale contracts need the developer's written consent to assign, and many charge an assignment fee. Some don't allow marketing an assignment on the MLS® until a set share of the project is sold. Read your contract first.
the assignee usually pays you back your deposit plus any profit (the "lift"), and pays the rest of the original price to the developer at completion.
your deposit stays with the developer's trust account and counts toward the purchase at completion.
on a new home, GST can apply both to the profit on the assignment and to the price at completion. Get tax advice before you list.

parts.t: Since January 1, 2025, BC has taxed profits on homes, and presale contracts, sold within two years (
Province of BC

items.t: the rate falls on a sliding scale.

parts.t: For an assignment, the clock generally starts when you paid the deposit and stops when the assignee pays you. Presale contracts don't qualify for the builder or renovator exemptions, and a return is due within 90 days of the sale. The federal residential property flipping rule can also treat a quick profit as business income, so talk to an accountant.

You get a nearly new home, often at a price set a year or two ago, with time before completion. Check the remaining deposit, the completion date, the strata disclosure statement and the developer's consent terms before you write an offer. Browse

honoring-indigenous-culture-xwepiteng-el.h1: Xw'epiteng Elementary: South Surrey's Outdoor Learning School

parts.t: In July 2024 I wrote that the former Hall's Prairie Elementary in South Surrey would reopen with a new name gifted by the Semiahmoo First Nation. Xw'epiteng Elementary has now run its outdoor, land-based program since the 2024-25 school year. Here's what families should know.

items.t: 18035 8 Avenue, South Surrey, in the rural area near Campbell Valley Park

the Xw'epiteng Outdoor Land-Based Learning Program. Students learn outdoors every day and cover the full B.C. K-7 curriculum, with Coast Salish culture, language and history built in. Teaching is inquiry-based, play-based and place-based, and students learn to manage risk outdoors (

parts.t: Xw'epiteng (pronounced roughly woh-pee-ten) means "place of many rabbits". The name was gifted by Semiahmoo First Nation Chief Harley Chappell, and the Surrey school board approved it in June 2024. The school had worked with the Semiahmoo for years before that, including changing its mascot to the hawk in 2009 after consulting the Nation.

Xw'epiteng isn't a typical neighbourhood school. Kindergarten spots go through the Surrey Schools online kindergarten lottery each winter, and families with children in Grades 1 to 7 contact the school directly. Because kindergarten places go by lottery, living nearby doesn't guarantee a spot. Ask the school about transportation before you count on it.
For families who want a nature-based education, the school adds to the appeal of South Surrey's rural pockets:
Hazelmere, Campbell Valley and the acreages along 8 Avenue and 16 Avenue.

south-surrey-highway-upgrades-advance-to.description: The 20 Avenue overpass of Highway 99 is under construction to December 2027, next to the new Costco. What's being built and what it means for homes.
south-surrey-highway-upgrades-advance-to.h1: South Surrey Road Upgrades: 20 Avenue Overpass and Highway 99

parts.t: In October 2025 I wrote that Surrey was moving ahead on two road projects around Highway 99 in South Surrey. One of them is now under construction. Here's the update, and what it means for the neighbourhoods around it.

items.t: a new 20 Avenue bridge over Highway 99 with four lanes (two each way) and a multi-use path for walking and cycling. It's an overpass, not an interchange: there are no ramps on or off Highway 99.
20 Avenue is being widened to four lanes between 160 Street and just before 164 Street.
construction started in early 2026 and is scheduled to finish in

parts.t: The overpass is tied to a new Costco on a 33-acre site at 1891-1947 164 Street: a 165,000 sq. ft. store, a gas station and 975 parking stalls, with more than 400 jobs. Costco is targeting a late 2027 opening. Together, the store and road work are a project of more than $100 million.

The second project, new north-facing ramps at the 24 Avenue interchange on Highway 99, is at a much earlier stage. In early 2026 the city described it as exploring additional ramps at 24 Avenue. Don't count on it when buying; treat it as a possible long-term improvement.

blocks.text: What it means for homes nearby

items.t: a second east-west crossing of Highway 99 at 20 Avenue should take pressure off 24 Avenue and 16 Avenue. That makes it easier to get between Grandview Heights, Morgan Creek and the shops along 152 Street.
Living close to the Costco site:
convenience for most, more traffic on 164 Street and 20 Avenue for those right next to it. If you're buying on one of those streets, look at the site plan and visit at a busy time.
expect lane closures and detours on 20 Avenue and around 164 Street.

new infrastructure and a major retailer are usually good for nearby values over time, but buyers will still discount homes right next to construction until it's finished. Timing your sale around that can matter.

tatalu-elementary-school-opening-earlier.title: Ta'talu Elementary, South Surrey: A Guide for Home Buyers
tatalu-elementary-school-opening-earlier.description: Ta'talu Elementary opened in Grandview Heights in October 2024: capacity, grades, features, and what it means for families buying in South Surrey.
tatalu-elementary-school-opening-earlier.h1: Ta'talu Elementary in Grandview Heights: What Buyers Should Know

parts.t: When I wrote about Ta'talu Elementary in May 2024, the school was running ahead of schedule. It opened on October 1, 2024, three months before its planned January 2025 start. Here's what families buying in Grandview Heights should know about it now.

items.t: up to 655 students. It opened with more than 220 students and 11 divisions (
a three-storey, 27-classroom hybrid mass timber school with a large gym, library learning commons, maker spaces and two rooms for child care.
an old-growth western red cedar beside the playground, a gravel field, an outdoor basketball court and preserved rocks and stumps for outdoor learning.
Ta'talu is SENĆOŦEN for "little arms", gifted by Semiahmoo First Nation Chief Harley Chappell. It refers to the Campbell River and its tributaries.

parts.t: Grandview Heights has grown faster than its schools for years. Ta'talu added hundreds of elementary seats close to the area's newer townhomes and detached homes, and it changed catchment boundaries for nearby schools when it opened.
That's why I always tell buyers:
check the catchment by address, not by neighbourhood name.
Catchment lines follow streets, and two homes a block apart can be in different schools. Use the Surrey Schools school locator, and read my
South Surrey school catchment guide
for how to check before you write an offer.
Being in a new school's catchment is a selling point. Homes within walking distance of Ta'talu tend to get more attention from families, especially townhomes with three bedrooms.

The streets around 165A Street and 20 Avenue are mostly newer detached homes, coach-house homes and townhome complexes. Nearby is the 20 Avenue overpass of Highway 99, under construction since early 2026 and scheduled to finish in December 2027, which will link Grandview Heights to the new Costco site on 164 Street.

transforming-langley-new-development-pla.title: Former Gabby's Site, Langley City: The Condo Plan Update
transforming-langley-new-development-pla.description: The condo plan for the former Gabby's site at 203 Street and Fraser Highway was cancelled in 2025. Where the corner stands, across from SkyTrain.
transforming-langley-new-development-pla.h1: The Former Gabby's Site, Langley City: The Condo Plan Update

parts.t: In March 2024 I wrote about a plan to replace the former Gabby's Country Cabaret in downtown Langley City with a six-storey condo building. That plan didn't go ahead. Here's what happened, and why the corner is still one to watch.
In April 2024 Kerr Properties applied to Langley City for a development permit at
20297 Fraser Highway
, the northwest corner of 203 Street and Fraser Highway. The proposal was a six-storey mixed-use building with
78 apartments
(one, two and three bedrooms) over
678 m² of ground-floor commercial space
, with bike parking for residents.
Gabby's had hosted live country music for years and appeared in TV shoots such as Riverdale. It closed during the pandemic in 2020 and the building was demolished in 2021.
The application went to Langley City's Advisory Design Panel on April 16, 2025. Langley City's development activity report then lists it as
"Application Cancelled" on May 2, 2025
Langley City, June 2025
). In late 2025 the 0.68-acre corner came up for sale as a development site, zoned C1 and inside the city's Transit-Oriented Core in the Official Community Plan.
Projects get cancelled for many reasons, from construction costs to financing and a slower condo presale market. It doesn't mean the site won't be built on.

items.t: Langley City Centre Station, the end of the Surrey-Langley SkyTrain line at 203 Street, is right across the street. Service is expected in late 2029. I cover the project in my
Langley City has a provincial target of 1,844 new homes over five years, and the downtown core is where most of them are planned.
more density planned around the station is generally good for land values, but it also means more construction nearby in the next few years.

urban-safari-rescue-centre-makes-progres.title: Urban Safari Rescue Society Reopens in South Surrey
urban-safari-rescue-centre-makes-progres.description: The Urban Safari Rescue Society at 1395 176 Street lost about 60 animals in a January 2023 fire. It has reopened to visitors; how to visit and help.
urban-safari-rescue-centre-makes-progres.h1: Urban Safari Rescue Society in South Surrey: Back After the Fire

parts.t: In March 2024 I wrote that the Urban Safari Rescue Society was getting close to reopening after a fire. It did: by November 2024 the rescue was welcoming visitors back (
Global News
). Here's the story and how to visit.

items.t: in late January 2023, a fire at the centre at
in South Surrey killed about 60 exotic animals and badly damaged the building.

through 2023 and 2024 the society got its building permits, passed its electrical inspection, and restored the smoke-damaged rooms with insulation, drywall and new fixtures, while it kept running outreach programs and caring for the surviving animals.
the reopening was paid for in large part by community donations.

parts.t: Urban Safari takes in exotic animals that people can no longer keep, such as reptiles, birds and small mammals, and uses them in education programs for schools, camps and community groups. Check the society's website for visiting hours, tours and summer camps before you go.

Donations, volunteering and booking a tour or a birthday party all support the animals. It's a good family outing in the rural part of South Surrey, close to Campbell Heights and the Hazelmere Valley.
